summary: Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia worked in Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as University Teacher for the Ph.D. in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Harvard and Yale, he taught at Silpakorn University, the University of Michigan, the University of Vermont, and served as curator at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College and Oriental College. He held positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, several museums, the Government of India, and served as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He taught as a lecturer and associate professor at Tohoku University and was attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University in 1974.

Hirofumi Toda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University from circa 1978 to 2001 and was affiliated with the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. Her career includes serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University, attested between 2013 and 2016.

Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Hiroshima University and the University of Leipzig (Dr. phil. 2019). She worked as research staff at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023) and joined the University of Vienna in 2024.

Hiromasa Tosaki was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyushu and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Satkari Mookerjee, among others. He was a professor at Kyushu University from circa 1978 to 1994.

Hiromi Habata is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held an academic career at Ryukoku University, attested as a lecturer in 1987 and affiliated in 2006.
Hiromichi Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Ryogon Fukuhara. He served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.
Hiromitsu Ikuma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from Tohoku University in 2019. He has served as a researcher at Taisho University and the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1945 to 1949 and later served as a professor there from circa 1968 to 1991.

Hironori Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University. He has held positions at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he was attested as a lecturer in 2026.

Hironobu Minami is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism in 2015 and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo around 1963. He served as a professor at Mie Chukyo University, attested in 1982.

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University from circa 1972 to 1983, taught at Morioka College (1983–1989), and served as a professor at Tohoku University from circa 2001 to 2019.

Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at International Christian University and the University of Southern California (Ph.D. 1998), he became a professor at Nanzan University in 1989.

Hiroshi Araki is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University and Osaka University, and served as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he was attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
